rivals.name: Councillor Prudence Stitchley
rivals.backAgain: Councillor Stitchley is back for another go. Same hat. She has had it brushed.
rivals.resignation: Councillor Stitchley won, then resigned to spend more time with her hat.

rivals.name: Silas Dunnock
rivals.backAgain: Silas Dunnock is back for another go. He is waiting politely on the step.
rivals.resignation: Silas Dunnock won, then resigned to spend more time with his doorbells. He has gone to answer one.

rivals.name: Philippa Setter
rivals.backAgain: Philippa Setter is back for another go. Her leaflet is a crossword. Nobody has solved it.
rivals.resignation: Philippa Setter won, then resigned to spend more time with her crosswords. Her notice was eleven across.

rivals.name: Leander Waft
rivals.backAgain: Leander Waft is back for another go. He has had the spoon engraved: AGAIN.
rivals.resignation: Leander Waft won, then resigned to spend more time with the Ceremonial Spoon. It is his turn to hold it.

rivals.name: Hortensia Mallowby
rivals.backAgain: Hortensia Mallowby is back for another go. The accordion is wearing a rosette.
rivals.resignation: Hortensia Mallowby won, then resigned to spend more time with her accordion. It was waiting, half open.

rivals.name: Fergus Noonday
rivals.backAgain: Fergus Noonday is back for another go. He arrived at noon exactly, by his own reckoning.
rivals.resignation: Fergus Noonday won, then resigned to spend more time with his sundials. The afternoons, mostly.

rivals.name: Professor Ozias Kalends
rivals.backAgain: Professor Kalends is back for another go. He has started on Thursdays.
rivals.resignation: Professor Kalends won, then resigned to spend more time with his calendars. Effective last Wednesday.

rivals.name: Ottoline Strop
rivals.backAgain: Ottoline Strop is back for another go. She has brought her own chair and a cushion for it.
rivals.resignation: Ottoline Strop won, then resigned to spend more time with her chairs. She has not yet chosen one.

rivals.name: Lettice Ringrose
rivals.backAgain: Lettice Ringrose is back for another go. She rang ahead to say so.
rivals.resignation: Lettice Ringrose won, then resigned to spend more time with her handbells. All twelve were consulted.

rivals.name: Aldous Mould
rivals.backAgain: Aldous Mould is back for another go. He says the heap has been building up to this.
rivals.resignation: Aldous Mould won, then resigned to spend more time with his compost heap. It had been expecting him.

rivals.name: Araminta Dovecote
rivals.backAgain: Araminta Dovecote is back for another go. A pigeon brought the news ahead of her.
rivals.resignation: Araminta Dovecote won, then resigned to spend more time with her pigeons. They had written to her.

rivals.name: Ivo Pharos
rivals.backAgain: Ivo Pharos is back for another go. He has brought a model lighthouse. It is switched on.
rivals.resignation: Ivo Pharos won, then resigned to spend more time with his model lighthouses. One needed a new bulb.

rivals.name: Honoria Lathe
rivals.backAgain: Honoria Lathe is back for another go. She has left a space in the tapestry for it.
rivals.resignation: Honoria Lathe won, then resigned to spend more time with her tapestry. It shows her winning, then resigning.

rivals.name: Quentin Furlong
rivals.backAgain: Quentin Furlong is back for another go. He played himself in. It took a while.
rivals.resignation: Quentin Furlong won, then resigned to spend more time with his harmonica. He played his notice.

rivals.name: Imogen Tessel
rivals.backAgain: Imogen Tessel is back for another go. She has done the edges.
rivals.resignation: Imogen Tessel won, then resigned to spend more time with her jigsaws of sky. It is going well, she thinks.

rivals.name: Rufus Pantry
rivals.backAgain: Rufus Pantry is back for another go. He tapped the glass before coming. It said 'fair'.
rivals.resignation: Rufus Pantry won, then resigned to spend more time with his barometers. All of them saw it coming.

rivals.name: Gertrude Ambling
rivals.backAgain: Gertrude Ambling is back for another go. She walked here. It took a week, by choice.
rivals.resignation: Gertrude Ambling won, then resigned to spend more time with her walking boots. They were waiting by the door.

rivals.name: Bartholomew Knapp
rivals.backAgain: Bartholomew Knapp is back for another go. You may have heard him arrive.
rivals.resignation: Bartholomew Knapp won, then resigned to spend more time with his yodelling. He announced it from a hill.

grandProjects.name: The Very Long Bridge
grandProjects.text: It crosses the river, then carries on, in case the river moves.

grandProjects.name: The National Ribbon Mill
grandProjects.text: Ribbon enough to open everything twice. The mill itself is opened daily.

grandProjects.name: The National Umbrella
grandProjects.text: It keeps the whole capital dry. Crispin Mizzle calls it a good start.

grandProjects.name: The Tallest Bandstand
grandProjects.text: No bandstand has ever stood higher. The band is still climbing.

grandProjects.name: The Ministry of Ministries
grandProjects.text: It oversees every ministry. A new ministry now oversees it.

list.name: Bandstand Summer
list.text: The band plays in every district this term. Brass carries further.

list.name: Committee Week
list.text: More committees come to the desk. They have formed one about it.

list.name: Quiet Press
list.text: The papers are full of pumpkins. Gossip struggles for the front page.

list.name: Ribbon Shortage
list.text: Ribbon is scarce this term. Each cutting costs more, and pleases more.

list.name: Kite Weather
list.text: A steady breeze all term. Kites, and the Kite Flyers' League, are up.

list.name: Market Fortnight
list.text: Fees bring in more this term. The fortnight lasts all term, as usual.

list.name: Early Doors
list.text: Visitors come sooner this term. Some are waiting before the door is open.

list.name: Hedge Inspection
list.text: The Tidy Hedge Committee counts for more. It has measured how much.

list.name: A Gentle Week
list.text: Saying nothing after a scandal is gentler. Rodney calls it resting.

list.name: Grievance Amnesty
list.text: Settling a boycott costs less. Cuthbert has a form for saying sorry.

papers.text: Grant the prize pumpkin the freedom of the town. It has asked very politely.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A ticket museum in the old ticket office. Then a ticket office for it.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Name the 7:02 bus after you, Mayor. It is late too, and also waves.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The clock tower's faces disagree. An inquiry will hear each face.
papers.subject: clocks
papers.biggerStudy: Both faces have spoken. The inquiry now wishes to hear the hands.

papers.text: Your signature on every bus ticket, Mayor. Each journey, approved.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will pay for a sign on the bakery: 7:02 EXPECTED SHORTLY.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Keep the pothole by the shoe shop. It is the 7:02's only stop.
papers.subject: potholes

papers.text: A hat for you, Mayor. The clock tower's is on order. No hurry.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it wants the spotters' bench. It has stood for weeks.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S HAT GIVEN SPOTTERS' BENCH; SPOTTERS STAND
clippings.refuse: HAT STILL STANDING. SPOTTERS SIT DOWN

papers.text: The bean rows hide a third of the 7:02. We want that third back.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Raise the 7:02's profile. A low stage outside the shops should do it.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Be photographed waiting for the 7:02, Mayor. Bring breakfast.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A working group on why tickets are so small. It will report on one.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The report no longer fits. The group asks for a season pass.

papers.text: Unveil the new timetable board, Mayor. Point at a likely time.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Move the prize pumpkin out of Till's Teas. People keep ordering it.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Our window says PAUSE AND ADMIRE. The 7:02 does both. Move the stop.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay to paint PROUDLY ADEQUATE on the bus station. Adequately.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We will hire the bus station wall. Then a bus. Then the queue.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Open our new window, Mayor. It does not open. Declare it anyway.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Sign to say our windows are windows, Mayor. We will frame it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A committee to word the OPEN sign. Two members favour AJAR.
papers.subject: signage
papers.biggerStudy: OPEN is agreed. The committee asks to begin on CLOSED.

papers.text: A committee to issue nose permits for shop windows. One nose each.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The nose committee asks to cover elbows too. And the odd forehead.

papers.text: A sign: SHOPS. Then MORE SHOPS. Then, at the bus stop, NOT BUSES.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: A sweeper for weigh-in days. Sweep one leaf, Mayor, for the camera.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A glass roof on the high street. Then glass sides. Then it is a window.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Signs at each end of the high street: THE MAYOR'S. ALSO THE MAYOR'S.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Put your face on the clock tower, Mayor. People check it every hour.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: 3 visitors in 4 come for the pumpkin. The fourth is lost. Signs?
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Open our compost bins by the bus stop, Mayor. Stand upwind.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Rodney promised our fence to the spotters. And to us, first.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Point the clock tower at the plots. Pumpkins it can see do 30 % better.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: The 7:02 may not hoot past the plots. Nor the 7:15. Nor the clock.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay for a parade permit. The parade is the pumpkin.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will pay to rename the bus stop PUMPKIN CORNER. It is not a corner.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We would hire the bus station's parcel scales. Ours are too kind.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Pose with the prize pumpkin, Mayor. Its good side, then yours.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Study the high street pothole. Its soil may be better than ours.
papers.subject: potholes
papers.biggerStudy: The soil is promising. The study now asks for a second pothole.

papers.text: A study of the prize pumpkin's admirers. So far: 312, and a heron.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.biggerStudy: The study is complete. It now asks to count those who looked away.

papers.text: A committee on where the 7:02 should look as it passes our plots.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: Settled: ahead. The committee now asks what it should think.

papers.text: Ask the vegetables what they think of you. 90 % have not objected.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A rain gauge for your desk. It is empty now, but one can hope.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the rain gauge: it wants the prize bed. Your desk is too dry.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S RAIN GAUGE GIVEN PRIZE BED
clippings.refuse: RAIN GAUGE SENT BACK, STILL EMPTY

papers.text: A bus-shaped bench by the shops. You sit at the front and look punctual.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Window boxes for the town hall. Flowers only. A leek has applied.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A show results board by the shops. Last year's results to follow.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A warm seat by the shops. Between us we have waited eleven years.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A plinth for the winner of Window Week. The winner is a window.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Cabbages round the bus stop, with a sign: QUIET, WE ARE GROWING.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A light by the plots for late buses. Pumpkins asked to be kept in the dark.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A high street glass case for the pumpkin. You would unveil it, slowly.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Awnings for the shops and the timetable. Cloud dims a window 30 %.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Let us sit in the Guild's window at bus times. We keep very still.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The Society's cold frames, for our hats. Sign: GROWN UNDER GLASS.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Turnips are 12 % more turnip in early spring. Move Window Week.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A right of way across the vegetable plots, from 8:14 to 8:16.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Two spotters for show day, to write down weights. Buses go unwritten.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The bus station waiting room, for Till's Teas. The customers are already seated.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay for the clock to chime at every bus: about forty a day.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: The pumpkin would like a spot in the hat window. It used the hat form.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: The bus stop is glass on three sides. By Guild rules, a window. Ours.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Till's Teas will pay to print the timetable, plus a tea break at 10:15.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will hire the high street on Sunday to read the timetable aloud. All of it.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Till's Teas will pay to sponsor the show cup. As a teacup.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will hire Till's Teas for the pumpkin's birthday. It is one.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the bus stop for seedlings. Then the shelter. Then a bus.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Present our prize for most buses seen, Mayor. Be pictured seeing one.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Say in public that the 8:15 ran on time. It nearly did.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Judge Window Week, Mayor. Admire each window, not yourself in it.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Our prize turnip asks for your name, Mayor. It has your bearing.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Attend the weigh-in, Mayor, and say 'goodness'. We will cue you.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A study of the founding napkin. A timetable may be on the back.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The napkin study found the timetable. It asks to find out if it still runs.

papers.text: We propose a study of why our last study took nine years. It should take about ten.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The study of the study recommends a third study, to be sure.

papers.text: What is a vegetable? A working group will take evidence at lunch.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The working group has taken its evidence. It asks a year more, for pudding.

papers.text: A committee to name the benches by the plots. Then one per bench.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The bench committee asks for a third bench, to hold its meetings on.

papers.text: A study of the seconds a passer-by gives a window. Three years.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The study found four seconds. It asks a year more to time the second glance.

papers.text: A review of the duck pond. So far: wet, ducks. Two more meetings.
papers.subject: ducks
papers.biggerStudy: Two more meetings were not enough. The ducks have asked to be heard.

papers.text: Your hats on show in the hall, Mayor, each with a plaque: WORN.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Name the duck pond after you. The ducks will be told in writing.
papers.subject: ducks

papers.text: Your portrait at every bus stop, Mayor, captioned PLEASE WAIT.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A desk fountain for you. It gets lonely. A friend on the high street?
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the fountain: it would like the Society's best rain barrel to drink from.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S DESK FOUNTAIN TAKES GROWERS' RAIN BARREL
clippings.refuse: DESK FOUNTAIN TOLD TO FIND ITS OWN WATER

papers.text: Another basket, to keep the first company. No reason, as before.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the second basket: it would like the top deck's front seat. Daily.

clippings.sign: BASKET TAKES FRONT SEAT OF TOP DECK; SPOTTERS LOG IT AS A PASSENGER
clippings.refuse: BASKET TAKES A LATER BUS

papers.text: A hat for Mondays. We have six more, one a day. No obligation.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it would like the Guild's front window. Centre, well lit.

clippings.sign: HAT TAKES GUILD'S BEST WINDOW; GUILD SPEECHLESS
clippings.refuse: HAT GOES BACK IN ITS BOX, SAYS NOTHING

papers.text: Bunting from the clock tower to every shop, at our cost. Buses may bow.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: Hang our bus portraits on the Guild's wall. Each sat, then left on time.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A rain barrel under the bus stop roof. It sheds the finest rain in town.
papers.subject: fountains

papers.text: A shop fountain, from the plots' rain barrel. You would open it, damply.
papers.subject: fountains

papers.text: Wear our rosette. Third prize, so nobody suspects favourites.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Is the allotment gate a shop window? A committee will look in.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The committee now asks whether the potting shed is a shop. It has a door.

papers.text: Move the weigh-in off the high street. Our windows are 40 % pumpkin.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A study in window-shopping: the pumpkin, wheeled past each window.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.biggerStudy: The study asks for a second lap. The pumpkin may have missed a hat.

papers.text: We will pay to name a bench after the pumpkin. Then the high street.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Remove the Society's PUMPKINS AHEAD sign. Ahead is the hatter's.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pose with a seed packet. Look as if you know what it grows.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A statue of you, Mayor, pointing modestly at something else.
papers.subject: statues

papers.text: A second bench at the bus stop. The first is 80 % notebooks.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay for a licence to stand by the shops. Leaning is a separate form.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Is the vegetable barrow a bus? It has wheels and a timetable.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The committee is split. It asks for a second barrow, to compare.

papers.text: An umbrella for your portrait. Then one for the frame. One never knows.
papers.subject: portraits

favour.text: About the umbrella: it would like the Society's potting shed. It is warm there.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S UMBRELLA GIVEN POTTING SHED
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLA LEAVES, FOLDED, WITHOUT COMMENT

papers.text: A spotters' square by your parking space. Half is bean rows.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A plaque by the shops where our first bus was logged. Lean on it, Mayor, nobly.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Turn the signpost to the depot. The shops know where they are.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: A working group to watch seedlings come up, from the spotters' bench.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.biggerStudy: The seedlings came up during the minutes. It asks for another spring.

papers.text: Point the Society's bench at the road. Pumpkins seen leaving since spring: 0.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Wear our badge for a day: ASK ME ABOUT WINDOWS. Be ready.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: An inquiry: do buses seen in shop windows count as sightings?
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry asks for a second window, to check the first.

papers.text: We will hire the photocopier: timetable, index, the index's index. Shops later.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Give the pumpkin the Guild's place in your photograph. It never blinks.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: Hire us the drawer FOR FURTHER STUDY, for seeds. Desmond's papers can budge up.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Boot scrapers for the shops. A third of the plots leave on boots.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A scarecrow for the patch, in your likeness. The crows are unconvinced.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A bus stop stands on our plot, unpermitted. Move it or plant it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A brass plaque for your parking space: HERE THE MAYOR ONCE PARKED.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A bottle of our finest fountain water. Next time, the fountain.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the bottled water: it would like to wash the Guild's windows. Thoroughly.

clippings.sign: FOUNTAIN WATER STREAKS GUILD WINDOWS; GUILD POLISHES ALL NIGHT
clippings.refuse: WATER SENT HOME IN ITS BOTTLE

papers.text: A signpost at the bus stop: SHOPS one way, SHOPS the other. To be fair.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Polish a shop window for the Drizzle. We chose the cleanest.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A file per bus, kept by the shops. Two buses have complained.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A survey of noses on our windows. So far, 60 % are yours, Mayor.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The nose survey asks for another year. You keep coming back.

papers.text: Let us log you like a bus: stop, wave, pull away.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A sign at the plots: PLEASE ADMIRE THE BUSES FROM ELSEWHERE.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: A portrait of you, Mayor, for the portrait of you in the hall. For scale.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A basket for the drawer FOR FURTHER STUDY. It gets peckish. Ribbons? No reason.
papers.subject: paperwork

favour.text: About the drawer's basket: the drawer would now like the bus timetable, to study.

clippings.sign: MAYOR FILES BUS TIMETABLE FOR FURTHER STUDY
clippings.refuse: DRAWER RETURNS BASKET, UNSTUDIED

papers.text: Move the spotters' bench. Our mannequins now wave at buses.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A doormat for you, Mayor: WELCOME, UMBRELLAS. Ever hopeful.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: The doormat asks for the hatter's doorway, where it is wetter.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S DOORMAT MOVES INTO HAT SHOP; HATS STEP OVER IT
clippings.refuse: DOORMAT STAYS PUT. STILL WELCOMING, STILL DRY

papers.text: Sunflowers round the patch, facing the road. For bees, mainly.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: We would like to make a display of you, Mayor. Tuesdays.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A carpet up the town hall steps, Mayor. And one for coming down.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the depot's spare bus as a window. It never leaves. Ideal.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Window boxes on the bus stop rail. Buses now 50 % geranium.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Switch on our bus counter, Mayor. The photograph waits for a bus.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: A study of the baker's window timetable. Then its footnotes. Then the baker.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The footnotes now reach the door. The study would like the door.

papers.text: Lend us the weigh-in judges' stand. We would stand on it and judge buses.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A framed rosette for you at each weigh-in, Mayor: ATTENDED.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Lend us the Hilltop bandstand for hats on stands. The pumpkins may watch.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: A goose came second at the weigh-in. Present its rosette, Mayor.
papers.subject: geese

papers.text: A fountain pen, for signing. Then a fountain for the pen. Then a square for it.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: The fountain pen asks to sign the bus timetable. Every page, in its best hand.

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S PEN SIGNS TIMETABLE; BUSES NOW ILLEGIBLE
clippings.refuse: FOUNTAIN PEN KEPT IN A DRAWER, CAPPED

papers.text: A bus-viewing deck on the Hilltop bandstand. Pumpkins may use the stairs.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Witness page one of our new notebook. Nothing has happened yet.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Can buses be seen from the patch? An inquiry will stand on it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The patch inquiry saw one bus. It asks for a crate, and a season, for the rest.

papers.text: A ribbon for your pen. Uncut. A small ceremony? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: The ribbon on your pen asks to enter the weigh-in. It is light, but keen.

clippings.sign: PEN RIBBON ENTERS WEIGH-IN; MAYOR CHEERS, PUMPKINS DO NOT
clippings.refuse: RIBBON NOT ENTERED. LIONEL SASH: 'NO REASON'

papers.text: We will pay for a sign on the weigh-in scales: AS SEEN IN OUR WINDOWS.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Lend us the baker's awning on weigh-in day. 3 pumpkins in 4 mind drizzle.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Lend us the bus stop timetable frame on Saturdays. Such glass.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We will hire the bus loudspeaker for the weigh-in. Then the soil report.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A queue rail at the hatter's, where spotters stand. No queue yet.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Stand at the bus stop with us, Mayor. Look keen. A bus may come.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An inquiry into the scales, at the bus stop. First, it weighs itself.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The scales inquiry got two weights. It asks for a second bus stop, to compare.

papers.text: A committee to add pumpkins to the founding napkin. Lightly.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The napkin committee has filled the napkin. It asks for a second napkin, and lunch.

papers.text: A banner over the high street: WEIGH-IN SATURDAY. BRING A PUMPKIN OR A VIEW.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We will pay to name each town hall step after a bus. 14 steps; 16 buses.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: The weigh-in on the bus forecourt, for a day. Buses can watch.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A committee on dusting pumpkins on show. Minutes kept and dusted.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The dusting committee asks for a second pumpkin, as a control, and a new duster.

papers.text: A kettle hook by the draper's. Then a shelf. Then a small kitchen.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Lend us the Guild's ladder. We look up to buses, properly.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A study: can a shop bell be heard over a bus? You will listen.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The bell study will now try every bus. You are to keep nodding.

papers.text: Rodney says you adore the weigh-in. Come and adore it?
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A sign at the bus stop: WAITING? SO ARE OUR HATS.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Your own bus stop, Mayor. Buses expected: none.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A town hall steps rota: the Guild till noon, then us. You get 1:00 to 1:05.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Runner beans down the high street. Then peas. Then the shops.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: We will hire the Hilltop bandstand for bus recordings. 90 % idling.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Lend us the patch on Sundays. Our hats need to get out more.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Launch our window on wheels, Mayor. It follows the weigh-in, politely.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Move band practice to the jetty. The fish have had it easy.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A fish census. So far: fourteen, or one fish fourteen times.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.biggerStudy: The fish census asks for a second canal, to keep the counted fish apart.

papers.text: A float-shaped bandstand, to welcome the Anglers. It faces them.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: The Anglers will hire one silent Sunday. Receipts to be whispered.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A canal bridge plaque: BUSES SEEN HERE TWICE, IF YOU COUNT THE CANAL.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Watch a float for the camera, Governor. Hold still; it will.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: 80 % of fish are mid-canal. A floating bench lets us join them.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Canal boats keep no timetable. A study will wait on the towpath for one.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: Still no timetable. The study asks for a boat of its own, to wait on.

papers.text: A sign on our jetty rail: NO LEANING. THE FISH FEEL LOOKED AT.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: We will pay for a boat licence for the prize pumpkin. It floats.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A jetty sign, facing the water: THE SHOPS ARE BEHIND YOU.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The band will hire a barge: a verse at each lock, the chorus at the top.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Name a lock after you, Governor. Pose on top as the boats rise to you.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: An umbrella for your pen. Then your hand. Rain is likely, they say.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the pen's umbrella: it would like to shelter the timetable. From readers.

clippings.sign: UMBRELLA COVERS TIMETABLE; NO BUS TIMES SEEN SINCE
clippings.refuse: TINY UMBRELLA RETURNED, NEATLY FOLDED

papers.text: Ride the first bus over the mended bridge. Front seat; look brave.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A study of canal-watered marrows. So far they are 98 % canal.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows
papers.biggerStudy: The marrow study asks for the canal itself, to rule out the cans.

papers.text: A jetty bell, to ring when the band is too loud. It is louder.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Turn the towpath benches to face the water. Then the bandstand.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: We would hire the canal's reflection. Without the shop windows.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Our cans seek a right of way to the canal. Each has a form.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: The canal bed is the province's last unplanted bed. May we?
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Cut our display's ribbon, Governor. Gently: it is the display.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: A committee to define 'gleaming'. Samples: the band's cornets.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Next: 'sparkle', 'shine' and 'glint'. It asks to borrow the drums too.

papers.text: A sign on every bus: THE GOVERNOR MAY BE ABOARD.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Move the band out of the bus station. 30 % of buses are logged as trombones.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Add your name to every founding napkin. There is room by the gravy.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: An inquiry into footprints in the marrow beds. They lead to the bus stop.
papers.subject: gardens
papers.biggerStudy: The footprint inquiry asks to follow the footprints onto the bus. All routes.

papers.text: Move the growers' show from bay four. The 8:15 stopped and came third.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The band wants to grow its audience. We suggest sunflowers.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Practice in the plots, please. Onions are 3 % happier after a waltz.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A bandstand in the arcade, by the hat shop. Then in the hat shop.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Face the Sunday band away from our windows. People are looking at the band.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A working group on standing ovations. It will sit in the bus station.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The ovations group asks to study encores next. Several, to be thorough.

papers.text: Felt under the bandstand; our windows hum. Then felt cornets, to be safe.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Lean on a spade for the camera, Governor. Do not dig; it shows.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Mention Till's Teas in a speech. We have marked three places.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will pay for a sign on the bandstand roof: HATS, ONE STREET OVER.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: A basket, with scissors, in case anything needs opening. No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the scissors: they would like to trim the Guild's awnings. Shorter.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR'S SCISSORS TRIM AWNINGS; HATS NOW IN FULL SUN
clippings.refuse: SCISSORS SENT BACK, STILL IN THE BASKET

papers.text: A shelter for the tuba alone, by the water. The band insists.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Pose with every bus in the province. One frame per bus.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A sign on the pond, for the growers: THIS IS NOT A WATERING CAN.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: The bandstand, for spotting: four stops; five if the band sits.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Conduct the band for one bar. One. We will tell you which.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A study of pumpkins in windows: one a display, two a show, three a harvest.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Four pumpkins now. The study asks for the shop next door.

papers.text: Bus times on every shop awning. Shade you can set your watch by.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The hat shop's window for the cornets this week. The tuba's next.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A hut out of earshot of the band. Cuthbert is measuring earshot.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Rename the river after you. You reflect well on 300 metres of it.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Receive the Brass Thimble on the steps. Hold it up, so it shows.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: The bandstand for our pumpkins in autumn. They listened all summer.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: We will sponsor the rests in the band's music. Our windows enjoy those.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Buses slow 9 % by the hat shop. A committee will ask the hats why.
papers.subject: hats
papers.biggerStudy: The hats have not answered. The committee will wait a year, outside.

papers.text: A copy of the founding napkin for our window. Pressed, for once.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A hat for the Ceremonial Spoon. One for its stand. One for you?
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: The spoon's hat asks to judge the shop windows. It has seen so many.

clippings.sign: SPOON'S HAT JUDGES WINDOWS; GOVERNOR HOLDS SPOON
clippings.refuse: HAT SENT BACK; SPOON BAREHEADED BUT CALM

papers.text: Move the bus stop off the bridge. We have looked up 212 times this spring.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A working group on whether an onion may be applauded, or only the band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Somebody clapped. The working group asks for a further year.

papers.text: Wear the beetroot's rosette for the photograph. It has agreed.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The band will hire the riverbank. The tuba will stay in its case.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Muffle the shop bells by the river. Unmuffling by written request.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: An inquiry into conducting. It will wave its arms by the canal, to learn.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry can now conduct. It asks for a band to practise on.

papers.text: A pair of ribbon scissors for you, painted gold. Engraved: NO REASON.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: The gilt scissors would like to judge the leeks. They have the eye for it.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR'S GILT SCISSORS JUDGE LEEKS; GROWERS SILENT
clippings.refuse: SCISSORS SENT BACK; GOLD PAINT STILL WET

papers.text: A corner of the riverbank for one bean row. The beans have plans.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Brass bunting for the high street. It does not flap. It clangs.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: Sit through the Quiet Competition. Rodney may take one quiet photograph.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A sign over the shops: BUS DUE SHORTLY. Shortly to be defined.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Give the Circle the band's Thursday. Bands welcome, empty-handed.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Your signature round the tuba. It continues on the euphonium.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A survey to confirm the river is still flowing. Monthly, from a bench.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Findings: it flows. A second year is needed to learn which way.

papers.text: The Circle's stools for our hats, please. The hats ask for footrests.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: The Circle will pay to name the 6:10. They would call it nothing.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will pay to name a shelter after our founder's notebook. 41,000 buses.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Leeks along the bus station roof. The buses never look up.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Wave at the 8:20. It will be logged as an official wave, in ink.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: We will hire the departure board on show day: ALL BUSES CALL AT THE MARROWS.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A working group on noise. It will meet in silence, so may take a while.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The working group on noise asks for a second room. The first one echoed.

papers.text: A sign by the prize beds: PUMPKINS AT WORK. TUBA BY APPOINTMENT.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: A practice room by the river. Thin walls, as requested.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: We will pay for top billing at the Sunday concert. Posters: PUMPKIN, WITH BAND.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Rodney promised us the riverbank. He promised the Anglers too.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A sign on the river bridge, for the buses: TIPTOE.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Your face on every jar of Glasshouse jam. Pruella will check each jar.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study: is a bus seen through the glasshouse seen, or grown?
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The study asks for a second bus, as a control. Results at harvest.

papers.text: A hat for your portrait, painted on. It will raise it to visitors.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: The portrait's hat asks to enter the Quiet Competition. It keeps very still.

clippings.sign: PORTRAIT'S HAT ENTERS QUIET COMPETITION; GOVERNOR'S FACE TOO LOUD
clippings.refuse: HAT WITHDRAWN; COMPETITION HELD IN USUAL SILENCE

papers.text: The timetable out of our window. In it: TIMES VARY. HATS DO NOT.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Give the Circle a minute. They will hand it back unused.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: An inquiry into glasshouse acoustics. Tomatoes to sit still.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry asks for another season. The first was mostly band.

papers.text: The prize pumpkin's own glasshouse, on the high street. Tomatoes talk.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A fern, for your desk. Then a pond for the fern. Then a fountain.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: The fern would like to enter the county show. It is nearly a vegetable.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR ENTERS FERN IN VEGETABLE SHOW; JUDGES POLITE
clippings.refuse: FERN STAYS ON DESK, STILL NEAR NO FOUNTAIN

papers.text: Is jam in a window a show entry? A working group is tasting it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The jam working group has reached the bottom of the jar. It asks for a second.

papers.text: Lend us the hat shop doorway. It sees nine bus stops and one hat.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A portrait in every county hall. I found you seven good sides.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: The weighing tent, for the Quiet Competition. Nodding by arrangement.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: An umbrella, just for you. Perhaps say 'rain' more in speeches?
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the umbrella: it would like a seat on the Bandstand Board. It has brought its own.

clippings.sign: UMBRELLA JOINS BANDSTAND BOARD; CONCERTS MOVED INDOORS
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLA LEAVES QUIETLY, STILL FOLDED

papers.text: Open Till's tea room at the bus station. One sip, for the camera.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the high street for our notebooks. They reach two lampposts.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Plant reeds by the bandstand. Reeds hear all and repeat nothing.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A fanfare per show winner, at our cost. Eight bars an onion, four a radish.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Lunch with the growers at the county show? I booked it for eleven.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A board by the shops of every bus logged. Then one for the footnotes.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Stand at the stop a minute. I will log you as a rare sighting.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The spotters' bench for the drum. Sign: RESERVED, DRUM.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An inquiry into nose prints on our windows, each filed by height.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry asks to call each pane as a witness. They saw it all.

papers.text: We will pay to name the growers' jam the 8:15. Strawberry, slightly late.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A survey: how far does a cornet carry over water? Ewan moves back each week.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The survey has reached the far bank. It asks for a wider river.

papers.text: A spotting step by the glasshouse. Buses look 20 % riper through it.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Till's Teas would hire the judges' table. Judging resumes after tea.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The band's Sunday, for a timetable reading. With an interval.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Glaze the bandstand with the growers' spare panes. Rain applauds.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Pose with the band, holding the cymbals. Do not, at any point, use them.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A Guild tent at the county show, so vegetables can window-shop.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Lend our show the towpath for a day. Pumpkins have never seen a boat.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The band will hire the arcade on Saturdays. Rattled windows get receipts.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Turn the bus stop round to face our windows. The road will keep.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Paint on the bandstand: CONCERT SUNDAY. ALSO THURSDAY. ALSO NOW.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Gild the bus stop to match us. Then the bus. Then the notebooks.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Move the Guild's sandwich board. From our stop, it looks like the 9:40.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The market on Sundays, to practise. Quietly, then the drum.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A band on a bus: a concert, or a bus? An inquiry will ride the 6:50.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The band-bus inquiry asks to ride every route. With the drum.

papers.text: Rodney wants your face on the side of every van. They will drive slowly.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A hat for your desk clock, and your lamp. The in-tray looks cold.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: The clock's hat asks to hang on the bus stop sign. It wants to be waited for.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR HANGS HAT ON BUS STOP; SPOTTERS WAIT FOR IT
clippings.refuse: HAT STAYS ON DESK CLOCK; TIME UNAFFECTED

papers.text: A bus shelter by the shops, for passing trade. Nine buses pass an hour.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The spotters' arcade bench, for hats. They will watch for buses.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Till's Teas would hire the show scales. Scones only; marrows by eye.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Turn the Guild's new sign to OPEN, Governor. We will photograph the click.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: A study of the growers' ounce. So far: three, all different.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The ounce study asks for more time. It has found a fourth.

papers.text: A cuckoo in the Provincial Clock to say your name. Another to agree.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: A basket of ribbon. The fruit was eaten on the way. No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the ribbon: on concert day, it would like to go round the bandstand.

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR TIES UP BANDSTAND; BAND PLAYS ON THE GRASS
clippings.refuse: RIBBON RETURNED, STILL IN ITS BOW

papers.text: Add to each county signpost, under BUS STATION: OR, THE SHOPS.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: For our window: the band's music stands. Then jackets. Then the band.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: We will pay to make the prize pumpkin a weight. A hat: 0.003 pumpkins.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Sign the prize onion's certificate. Bertram confirms: an onion.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A bus stop right beside the bandstand. Every tune gets a bus in it.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A signpost to you in every county. Then one on you, saying HERE.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will hire an allotment corner. Spotters to register as leeks.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Stop the Provincial Clock on show day. Growers need more time; buses, less.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: The band will pay to list practice as an event. Wrong notes free.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Ring the concert bell for the camera. Then stay to the end.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A study: the band is 30 % quieter than it sounds. To be played.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The quiet study wants a louder edition. Nobody heard the first.

papers.text: A plaque where the pumpkin grew: SHE GREW HERE. KINDLY KEEP OFF.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Lend the band the bus shelter on Sundays. Its audience is waiting.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: An inquiry: why does the show page follow the bus page? It reports after them.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry now asks for its own page. It would like to go first, for once.

papers.text: Hold our ceremonial float for the Evening Fuss. Neither of you may bob.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Is the bus horn in tune? A study will audition each bus.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: The auditions ask for a second round. Several buses were nervous.

papers.text: A bandstand clock, so the band sees when to stop. Facing the audience.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Pose waiting in the new shelter. The 9:14 has been asked to hurry.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A committee on the echo. Its sign: ECHO, PLEASE WAIT YOUR TURN.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The echo committee asks to meet twice. Once, then slightly later.

papers.text: We will buy the five o'clock chime, to keep. The band starts on it.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: One bus horn a day at the river bridge. We will pick the honk.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Add QUIET, BAND to each county signpost. Small, as an example.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pad the river bus shelter. A pencil carries 40 metres over water.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Build Kitecombe a hill. The League currently launches from a chair.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: New string for the League. 61 % of the old string is in hedges.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A topiary kite on the kite field. Then its string, then its flyer.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Declare the Kitecombe maze kite-free. The kites in it will be told, once found.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A sign over the water, facing up: KITES, PLEASE GO ROUND.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: New shears for the Committee. The anglers' willow is worried.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Roof the spotters' bench. Last year it logged 30 % kites.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Lend the League the band's hill on kite day. The valley echoes nicely.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Pose beside a hedge clipped in your likeness. A modest hedge.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Let the Guild arrange the hedges as a display. The Committee did them first.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The Circle will pay for band practice indoors. Far indoors.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Awnings for the shop windows, printed: THIS IS NOT A LANDING.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: A net over the marrow beds. Last year a kite came second.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Judge the hedge show. All 212 are straight, so point at one and smile.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: An inquiry into why coaches come in threes. Three copies, in the Guild's window.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Three more coaches came. The inquiry asks for three more windows.

papers.text: Ride the first coach of spring. You will be logged as luggage.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Hold the marrow show in the coach park. Parked coaches get weighed.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A committee to pick a tune, on the kite field. It will hear every tune first.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The tune committee heard every tune. Now it asks for an encore.

papers.text: The band would like a hearing. A sound shell by the water will do.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A sign on every hedge: KITE CUSHION. The hedges were not asked.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: The band will pay for a licence to echo. Anglers hear each tune twice.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Lend a shop window the founding napkin. The Guild will iron it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A study of silence by the water. So far: 70 % quiet, 30 % band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The silence study needs a quieter room. It asks for the band's.

papers.text: The spotters will pay to stand in the marrow beds. Then to sit.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A working group to tie up loose ends: the kite strings in hedges.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The loose-ends group is stuck in a hedge. It asks for a rescue group.

papers.text: Be photographed waving from every coach. All of them, one a day.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Give the band's Sunday hour to the Circle. Same hour, fewer notes.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A hat for you. And one for your coach. And for each wheel, perhaps?
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it asks to be logged by the spotters as a coach.

clippings.sign: SPOTTERS TOLD TO LOG A HAT; HAT RUNS LATE
clippings.refuse: HAT IS NOT A COACH, PRESIDENT RULES

papers.text: The Guild will pay for a quiet day. Each tune rattles eleven panes.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Rodney has clipped your signature into a hedge. He proposes the rest.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Rename the riverbank BANDSTAND (TEMPORARY) on Thursdays. Fish informed.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Survey the hedges with kite string, pulled tight. The League lends it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The string is not straight. The survey asks to survey the string.

papers.text: The growers will hire the kite field. Kites that land will be judged.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Lend the spotters a shop window. Coaches look better framed.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Pose with the prize onion for its portrait. Slightly behind it.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The League pays per kite fetched from hedges. The hedges hold 41.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A basket for the new President. Bigger than the first. The same no reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the basket: it would like a shop window. The Guild's best one.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S BASKET TAKES GUILD'S BEST WINDOW
clippings.refuse: BASKET REFUSED A WINDOW; TO BE EATEN INSTEAD

papers.text: A working group on what a marrow is. It meets on the kite field.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Some marrows may be courgettes. The marrow group asks for a sub-group.

papers.text: A doorstep fountain for you. It only runs when someone is watching.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the fountain: it is lonely. It asks to live by the anglers' water.

clippings.sign: FOUNTAIN MOVES TO RIVERBANK; ANGLERS TOLD NOT TO WATCH IT
clippings.refuse: FOUNTAIN STAYS ON DOORSTEP; RUNS ONLY FOR THE POSTMAN

papers.text: The Committee will pay to trim the hedge spotters lean on. Leaning rescheduled.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A window in the hedge, for one hat. The hedge will hardly notice.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Give the band kite day. And the day after, for the encores.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: First prize at every show. Cuthbert has entered you as an exhibit.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will pay to put the timetable in one shop window, the footnotes in six.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Call it the Hedge and Kite Show. Our kites are in it anyway.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The band will hire a shop window. Display: ONE CORNET, IN USE.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: The band's polishing day, for Window Week. Brass and glass cannot both shine.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: An inquiry into 'mild' in kite forecasts. Onions want it defined.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The onions are content. They would now like 'fairly' looked into.

papers.text: Clip the kite field hedge into a clock. Accurate to the nearest season.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: An inquiry into why kites land on buses. It will sit on the top deck.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry has outgrown the top deck. It asks for a second bus.

papers.text: Give the onion show the dry Saturday. Kites get the next, in spring.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Ladders for the hedges of Gusting Heights. 31 kites are waiting.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A desk fountain. It gurgles when you are right. It never stops.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: Your desk fountain has entered the hedge show. It expects to win.

clippings.sign: FOUNTAIN ENTERS HEDGE SHOW; GURGLES THROUGHOUT, IS UNPLACED
clippings.refuse: FOUNTAIN SENT BACK. IT HAS NOT GURGLED SINCE

papers.text: The band has our Thursdays by the lake. Now Fridays. One back, please.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Ribbon offcuts, to practise on. Any openings coming up? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the offcuts: they would like to be tied round every shop door handle.

clippings.sign: OFFCUTS TIED ON SHOP DOORS; NOBODY CAN GET IN
clippings.refuse: OFFCUTS RETURNED UNCUT. MR SASH 'NOT UPSET'

papers.text: We will pay to fly over the hedge show. Each kite has signed: I WILL NOT LAND.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A study of how far the band carries: from the lake, then the next lake.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The band study asks to listen from a third lake, to be thorough.

papers.text: We will sponsor the kite festival if kites keep in line. We drew the lines.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Sit with the anglers, for the front page. The band will whisper.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: The League would like to hire the wind over Brassby. They will pay.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Log a coach for the camera at the milliner's. It is already logged.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A kite festival working group. Item one: move the hedges.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The festival group must meet again. The hedges did not attend.

papers.text: A lid for the national bandstand. With a hole, for applause.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Wear our rosette to the kite festival. Onion morale is up 3 % already.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: A barometer for your desk. It only ever says RAIN.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the barometer: it wants the 8:15 held until it has decided.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT HOLDS 8:15 FOR BAROMETER; SPOTTERS LOG DELAY
clippings.refuse: BAROMETER SENT BACK. IT SAW THIS COMING

papers.text: Move kite day away from the lake. Last year our floats took off.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Kites landed in the onion beds 12 times. The onions flinch. A net, please.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: An inquiry into the shape of the wind. We would like it squarer.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry could not find the wind's corners. It asks to look again in autumn.

papers.text: Spotters lean on our hedge. Then picnics. Now a stepladder. Move the stop.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A ramp on Gusting Heights. The band is sitting on the good wind.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A committee to decide where a window ends and a spotter begins. Chalk provided.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The chalk line has been leant off. The committee asks for paint.

papers.text: Your speeches in gilt, beside the founding napkin. The napkin reads better.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Launch the season's first kite. Let go when we say. Not before.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A bandstand by the lake. The anglers have gone very quiet.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Every forecast to end with you. 'Light winds, then the President.'
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: An onion bed on the bandstand lawn. Dig the first hole, for the camera.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Kites land at the bus stop three times a day. Buses, twice.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A plaque on the draper's window: THE 8:15 WAS ON TIME HERE, ONCE.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pose by our best window. It covers the bus timetable entirely.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the 8:15 on show day. Onions only, one per seat.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Dim the lighthouse so the fish can sleep. The band reads its music by it.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The hat show asks for the kite field. Hats fly too, briefly.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Let us hire the arcade's glass roof. A bus is 12 % more bus from above.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A practice hut by the anglers, labelled SOUNDPROOF (MOSTLY).
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Present the Quiet Competition cup. Applause will be by eyebrow.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A marquee for our show, over the bus stop. Buses may enter as exhibits.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Hold our spool for the camera. The kite is in the next province.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: An inquiry: is a kite in the bay a fish? If so, nobody may pull it out.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The kite-or-fish inquiry wants a second summer. The kite is still in.

papers.text: Your face on the new stamp. Mildred has seen three, and kept one.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: Register every hedge: name, age, and any kite it is holding.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The holiday bunting, on our windows this year. The bus station has had nine years.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Lend our prize onion the hat in the Guild's window. Then gloves.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: We will pay to name the new holiday WINDOW DAY, not TIMETABLE DAY.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A study of ripples in Saltpenny Bay. So far, 40 % are the band's.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.biggerStudy: The ripple study would now like the waves. Ewan has a second pencil.

papers.text: A shop window on the pier. The sea has never been shown a hat.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Sit for the new coin: heads, you. Tails, a bus, not a shop bell.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: We will hire the Quiet Competition's interval. Then the rest of it.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: An inquiry into the kite on the Guild's awning. It will speak from there.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The awning inquiry asks for a second season. The kite has not answered.

papers.text: Give us the top deck's front seat. Kites fly 30 % higher from it.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Open the hedge show. The ribbon is a hedge; shears provided.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the bandstand for the onion parade. Wave as they roll.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The band asks for the harbour steps. Anglers may keep the wet ones.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Pin the first-prize rosette on the onion. Rodney has one for you.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A committee to date the new holiday. It meets only on holidays.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The holiday committee needs more holidays to meet on. Three, to start.

papers.text: Choose the band's encore at the bay. Same tune again, but yours.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A hat with a smaller hat on it. The smaller hat has a request.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: The smaller hat asks for a place in the kite festival. It will need a string.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT FLIES HAT AT KITE FESTIVAL; KITES UNIMPRESSED
clippings.refuse: HAT REQUEST FILED FOR FURTHER STUDY

papers.text: We will hire the harbour for the holiday: 88 % quiet, 12 % goose.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A kite museum. The hedge outside holds most of the exhibits.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Hedge day and kite day clash. Ours was filed first, in triplicate.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A fanfare for each harbour ribbon. Scissors up on the last note.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A willow on the quay to sit under. The Committee may admire it.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A ceremony for your hundredth ceremony. First, a rehearsal ceremony.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Be our window display for an hour. Your card: PRESIDENT, ONE ONLY.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A picnic chair, with an umbrella and a spare umbrella. No reason.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the chair: it would like the front row at the show. Umbrella up.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT GIVES CHAIR FRONT ROW; GROWERS STAND
clippings.refuse: CHAIR SENT BACK; UMBRELLA STAYS UP, JUST IN CASE

papers.text: A study: do onions grow to brass? The band plays to them nightly.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The onion study wants a second bed, as a control. The band will play to both.

papers.text: A plaque at the harbour bus turn: BUSES TURN HERE. It goes on the shop door.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Clip the bus stop hedge into a bus. Then a queue. Then a late one.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Make your birthday a national holiday. Mildred has a drawer for these.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Hedge manners: a committee. Chapter one: may spotters lean? Two: no.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The manners committee wants a second volume: bowing to topiary.

papers.text: Move the harbour bus stop. Each horn undoes 40 minutes of quiet.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A motorway bench, where the hedge is, to watch coaches go by. They mostly do.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An extra hour on show day, from the National Clock. Spotters can spare one.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Lampshades for the street lamps. Then tassels. The bus stop's gets both.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Give us the League's telephone. We only ring for early coaches. Twice a year.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Tune one foghorn to the band. Then all of them. Then book a fog.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: We booked the bandstand on the band's form. Instrument: pumpkin.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A bandstand on wheels, to go to the audience. It is at the kites.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Till's Teas will sponsor the motorway lamps, in tea colour. Milky.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pose by our ten-thousandth coach. Lean on the hedge, as we do.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An arcade sign: PRIZE PUMPKIN, THIS WAY. It points outside.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Lend us the spotters' footbridge. Coaches are a loyal audience: they never miss a Sunday.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Light the pumpkin patch for night spotting. The pumpkins may not sleep.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Kites get the harbour wall. Anglers may apply to sit on the water.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Cushion the harbour wall, for the echo. Then the bandstand. Then the band.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A kite that lands in a hedge now belongs to it. Form attached.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Hear the harbour band by telephone, for the camera. Nod.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A lake lighthouse, for floats at dusk. It goes in the marrow bed.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Lamp-post signs: KITES MAY REST HERE. In place of SHOPS THIS WAY.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Trim the arcade hedge. Then the awnings, to match. Then the hats.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Dim the Guild's harbour windows at dusk. The water is 40 % hat.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The band will hire a lighthouse to play from. One bar per step, up to the top.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Unhook the telephones for the Quiet Competition. Till's Teas is ringing.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will pay to keep the bandstand in trim. Shears are packed.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Walk the arcade with the band, carrying cymbals. Carrying only.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A landing circle by the marrows. Kites miss circles by 3 metres.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay to put the pumpkin on the motorway signs. Coaches may follow it.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Launch a kite named after you. Smile before it finds the hedge.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay for dark harbour lamps at concerts. The band knows 30 % by heart.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A study: is a coach late if nobody waits for it? The Guild is asked to wait.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lateness study asks the Guild to wait at every stop, in turn.

papers.text: Your face on the National Clock. At noon both hands point at you.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study of marrows by lamplight. Half the high street goes dark, as a control.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The marrow study now needs the lit half dark, and the dark half lit.

papers.text: A desk lamp. It glows near ribbons. Any openings soon? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the lamp: it would like a solo at the Sunday concert.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S LAMP GIVEN SOLO; BAND PLAYS IN THE DARK
clippings.refuse: LAMP STAYS ON THE DESK, GLOWING AT NOTHING

papers.text: Light up the hedge show for the camera. Kites stay down until you smile.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A study on the lighthouse window display. Shortlist: LIGHT, LIGHTHOUSE.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lighthouse study now wishes to dress the beam. In stripes.

papers.text: Flash your initials from a lighthouse. Then your name, all night.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study: is a humming kite an instrument? If so, it joins the band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The kite study asks to hear a whistling kite, and one that sighs.

papers.text: A plaque on each lamp: LIT BY THE PRESIDENT. I have done four.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Does the anglers' willow need permission to droop? A study.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The willow study asks to inspect every willow for drooping.

papers.text: Three small umbrellas, one per telephone. Bad lines are so damp.
papers.subject: vanity

favour.text: About the umbrellas: they wish to judge the marrow show. Open.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S UMBRELLA JUDGES MARROWS; GROWERS DAMP
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLAS STAY BY THE TELEPHONES, OPINIONS UNSHARED

papers.text: Kites land on awnings. A study finds 9 in 10 prefer stripes.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The awning study asks to try plain awnings too. And spots.

papers.text: Glaze the park's bean rows. Then price cards. Then a shop bell.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A study of the band's quietest tune. Of 40, the interval leads.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The tune study asks for a longer interval, to be thorough.

papers.text: Hedge the park's coach turning circle. Coaches will learn to turn square.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A study of the 900 park benches. 3 face a road. The rest, hedge.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The bench study needs a second sitting. Some benches were taken.

papers.text: Go window-shopping, for the camera. We have wrapped you a window.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: The hedge show wants the marrow show's day. Hedges do not wilt.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Open the coach stop cut into the park hedge. Stand in for the coach.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The anglers have had 211 still evenings. The band would like one.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Tour the provinces with the national pumpkin. Front seat. Wave second.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The Ribbon Mill's first ribbon. Uncut. It could open something? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the ribbon: it would like to lead the Sunday concert.

clippings.sign: RIBBON LEADS BAND; BAND FOLLOWS, PUZZLED
clippings.refuse: RIBBON STAYS IN ITS BOX, UNCUT AND UNSURE

papers.text: Mow a kite runway by the coach stop. Ours have nowhere to taxi.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A sign on your fountain, paid for: COACHES, THIS WAY. It used to say SHOPS.
papers.subject: fountains

papers.text: A study: are the park's leek beds straight enough to be beds?
papers.subject: gardens
papers.biggerStudy: The bed study asks to inspect each leek row from a ladder.

papers.text: Print CUT BY THE PRESIDENT on every Ribbon Mill ribbon. Before you cut it.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: Tin cufflinks: two small fountains in your shape. A tie pin follows.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the cufflinks: they would like a seat at the Quiet Competition.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S CUFFLINKS JOIN QUIET COMPETITION; SPLASH, ASKED TO LEAVE
clippings.refuse: CUFFLINKS KEPT IN A DRAWER, STILL RUNNING

papers.text: The marrows have had the band's front row since the napkin. Move them.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A study of the Ribbon Mill's next shade. 40 beiges so far, each held up by the band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The shade study wants 40 more beiges. Two of the first matched.

papers.text: Unveil the national pumpkin's arcade plinth. Bow after it does.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will pay to judge your lawn's edges. Kites off it, pending.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A bandstand on the kite field. Its roof is a lovely place to land.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Lend us a corner of the hedge show lawn. Kites need very little. At first.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A Ribbon Mill window display: RIBBON, BEING MADE. Rosettes, round the back.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: A fountain in your shape. Rodney asks for a smaller one, for the fountain.
papers.subject: fountains

papers.text: Fly the motto on a kite: PROUDLY ADEQUATE. It flies about that well.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Move the spotters' bench. Our hedge now has a bench-shaped gap.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Your signature in gilt at the top of every form. The forms now start lower.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Cut the ribbon on our new notebook. Small scissors have been found.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: We will pay for a still lake. Reflected kites must apply.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A study of where the band stands. It is standing in the arcade.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The standing study stood in the arcade all summer. It asks for chairs.

papers.text: Turn your fountain to the arcade. It has seen enough marrows.
papers.subject: fountains

papers.text: Ribbon Mill tails for every kite: a metre, then two. Hedges get the rest.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: Keep time for the band's lake concert. Rodney will frame it.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Form 7 of the Republic is for coaches. The Guild keeps filing hats on it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: We will pay to keep the park hedges in shape. Ours: a hat.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Feed the ducks at the Quiet Competition, for the camera. Mime the crumbs.
papers.subject: ducks

papers.text: We will hire the growers' bean canes at night. Kites sleep upright.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Swap the lake hedge for a bench. 3 fish in 4 ask who is there.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A study of the kite form. Its one box says NO, in the Committee's hand.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The study asks for a form to add a box. That form has no box either.

papers.text: Growers water from our lake: a can, a hose, a pump. It is one duck deep.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Swap the park benches for hedge, clipped as benches. Rodney sat on one.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A shed for the prize pumpkin, right where the spotters stand.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A spotting step outside the shops, to rise above the glass.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Mervyn's bus so far: a bench, a roof, a timetable. Fund wheels?
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: A timetable in each shop window. 60 % of buses are missed at the cakes.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A form for window-shoppers. Tick one: LOOKED, LINGERED, LEANT.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A pane in front of each window, for leaning on. Then a pane for that pane.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Fund Bertram's new watering can. So far: 40 plants, two spotters.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Turn the shop hats round. They watch our buses and take no notes.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: The timetable case for our display. Its notice: TIMES ON REQUEST.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Lend us the shop awnings in drizzle. We will stand still, like a display.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: Let us polish the potting shed window. We have our own hat stand.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: A duck has applied to nest in our seed trays. Refer it to a window box.
papers.subject: ducks

papers.text: The flower bed by the shops, for leeks. Its sign: FLOWERS, EVENTUALLY.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: We will pay for you to open the allotment from our window. The leeks can see.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: We would hire the bus stop to show lost umbrellas: PLEASE DO NOT CLAIM.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: We will pay to grow the timetable in cress. Accurate until lunch.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: We will hire a window seat for spotting: the baker's, facing the stop.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Pose by Delphine's self-cleaning window as it works. Allow all day.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Wear our carrot hat. Rodney says it suits you. He says that of all hats.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Our calendar: you at the stop, checking a watch. We can lend one.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Lost property is up 40 %: one glove, handed in five times.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The study found the other glove. It asks to study the pair.

papers.text: A working group: is the timetable a form, and must buses fill it in?
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: No bus has filled it in. The group asks for a clerk at each stop.

papers.text: A study of pens that do not write. It will report in a spotter's pencil.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The study needs a second pencil. The spotters want the first one back.

papers.text: Plant the first bean for the camera. Bertram will replant it.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A standing committee on window pumpkins. It will stand by one.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: It now asks for chairs. Standing has been studied enough.

papers.text: A working group on picnic weather: nine meetings, one picnic.
papers.subject: picnic-weather
papers.biggerStudy: Still unsure. It asks for a second picnic, and a blanket.

papers.text: Permits for each window you were reflected in. Framed. I counted.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Your name on each rosette. Then the cup. Then, quietly, the show.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: An umbrella, left at your desk. Not forgotten: left. For when it rains.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the umbrella I left: it would like to be listed as a bus stop.

clippings.sign: UMBRELLA LISTED AS BUS STOP; NO BUS STOPS AT IT
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLA NOT A STOP. IT WAITS BY THE DESK

papers.text: Matching hats for you and the pumpkin. No reason. Lionel said to say that.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About my gift: both hats would like a place on the prize table, beside the pumpkin.

clippings.sign: HATS TAKE PRIZE TABLE; PUMPKIN WEIGHED ON THE FLOOR
clippings.refuse: HATS REFUSED A TABLE. THEY ARE, OFFICIALS NOTE, HATS

scripted.text: Practise on this one. It is a form about forms. File it FOR FURTHER STUDY.
Welcome, Mayor. Please sign this to say you have read it. You haven't. Sign it.
Let Till's Teas sponsor the clock tower. It would chime TILL'S TEAS on the hour.
A small fruit basket for you. No reason. Perhaps more ribbon-cuttings? No reason.
Welcome, Governor. Your mug says GOVERNOR. Mine says HOME TIME.
Welcome, President. I have welcomed three. I liked one.

afterSign.text: A study, please: since the band came, 3 fish in 4 nod along.
afterSign.subject: harbours

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR FUNDS STUDY OF FISH IN FOUR-FOUR TIME
clippings.refuse: STUDY SHELVED; FISH STILL NODDING ALONG

afterRefuse.text: The band wrote you a piece: 'Further Study'. Mostly rests.
afterRefuse.subject: bandstands

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR APPLAUDS DURING THE RESTS
clippings.refuse: 'FURTHER STUDY' PLAYED TO AN EMPTY CHAIR

afterSign.text: The band asks for a loud Monday, to balance your silent Sunday.
afterSign.subject: ceremonies

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR SPENDS LOUD MONDAY IN A CUPBOARD
clippings.refuse: LOUD MONDAY MOVED TO A QUIETER DATE

afterRefuse.text: Then sit by the canal with us and say nothing. Rodney is worried.
afterRefuse.subject: ceremonies

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR SILENT FOR AN HOUR; AIDES CONCERNED
clippings.refuse: ANGLERS SIT IN SILENCE, AS USUAL, WITHOUT GOVERNOR

afterSign.text: The bench drifted two locks, to where growers water. Anchor it?
afterSign.subject: inventions

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR'S ANCHOR HOLDS BENCH IN THE WRONG PLACE
clippings.refuse: FLOATING BENCH CONTINUES ITS TOUR OF THE PROVINCE

afterRefuse.text: Then we survey the fish on where to sit. The band hushes for replies.
afterRefuse.subject: inventions
